card.title: Composure on Loan
card.instruction: Project steady control while quietly depending on everyone else to stay calm enough for you to maintain it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding's under control. Tell me about the cake in that lovely calm voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's leaning. I can hold the stand level.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A minor adjustment. Keep talking like that while you hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll have to help. My hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll steady it together. You count us in; your voice hasn't started shaking.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares wedding control while requesting B's calm delivery, A3 praises the adjustment and sustained voice, and A5 needs B's steady count even while helping.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's leaning-cake solution informs A3's calm adjustment framing; B4's shaking hands make A5 join physically while borrowing the still-steady voice.

relationship.evidence: B2 takes useful action to hold the stand and B4 asks for help when that becomes difficult.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's distinction between unstable hands and continuing speech to preserve borrowed calm during joint repair.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies the wedding and B2 specifies the leaning cake and stand.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's voice-has-not-started-shaking line arises from B4's exact physical problem, without a separate gag.
